module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock FPGA controller wrapper that composes register access, bounded request/response transport, safety enforcement, and actuator limiting without implementing the external surrogate model.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use the register map as the sole source of configuration and status semantics, route transport handshake/data through the mandated valid/ready directions, and combine transport validation with actuator-safe fallback so any invalid, stale, timed-out, or faulted condition deterministically drives the safe command path.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain only the minimum synchronous state needed for configuration storage, outstanding request tracking, watchdog timing, response freshness/ID checking, sticky fault accumulation, and clamped actuator selection; keep all state reset-deterministic and avoid unnecessary FSM complexity.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive cfg_ready/cfg_rdata/cfg_rvalid from the register plane, drive req_valid/req_data outward and rsp_ready as a real output, and drive act_cmd/act_enable plus telemetry from validated or fallback-selected command results, with clamp and fallback indicators reflected as status.
ownership_notes: Owns the externally visible contract and integrates the three subfunctions without redefining hierarchy or ports.
Must preserve the requested transport directionality: request valid/data are outputs, request ready is input; response valid/data are inputs, response ready is output.
Must keep rsp_ready as a top-level RTL-driven output, not a pass-through from a child input.
Must not expose geometry arrays, tensors, flow fields, or surrogate internals.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_register_map
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small synchronous 32-bit register window with 8-bit addressing and direct semantic decode for control, limits, timeout programming, counters, and sticky fault readback.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Qualify all access with cfg_valid and the corresponding read/write strobes, decode addresses into named control fields, and update status/readback fields only on accepted operations or from explicit telemetry inputs.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Store enable, clear_faults, operating_mode, stream_velocity_setpoint, timeout_cycles, stale_age_limit, actuator_min, actuator_max, fallback_command, counters, and sticky fault bits in deterministic resettable registers; keep unsupported-address behavior simple and synchronous.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Provide cfg_ready, cfg_rdata, and cfg_rvalid deterministically for the selected address, and present decoded control outputs directly to downstream blocks without hidden interfaces.
ownership_notes: Owns the control-plane register file and its readback behavior.
Owns the semantic control outputs used by transport and actuator logic.
Consumes transport/status telemetry for status mirrors and sticky-fault management but does not drive transport pins directly.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_transport
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Bounded 64-bit streaming formatter/parser with minimal request descriptor handling and compact response validation logic, optionally backed by inferred block RAM or a small FIFO only if timing closure requires storage.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Emit outbound request metadata only after configuration enables operation, accept requests via req_valid && req_ready, capture the accepted transaction ID, start the watchdog, and parse inbound responses for ID match, freshness, and field legality before marking a candidate command valid.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Track a request-pending bit, outstanding transaction ID, last response ID, watchdog age, response age, parser error, candidate validity, and fallback indication with simple synchronous counters/flags; avoid complex FSMs beyond the natural request/response lifecycle.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive req_valid/req_data outward, consume req_ready as input, consume rsp_valid/rsp_data as inputs, and drive rsp_ready as a real output; produce candidate_cmd/candidate_valid only when response validation succeeds, otherwise select fallback behavior and assert safety status.
ownership_notes: Owns the request/response transport handshake and validation path.
Owns request-pending, watchdog-expired, response-age, last transaction IDs, candidate command, candidate validity, fallback indication, parser error, and fault status outputs.
Must not drive act_cmd or act_enable directly.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_actuator
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Simple combinational-plus-registered actuator safety block that selects validated command or fallback, clamps to programmed bounds, and optionally applies a small bounded transition policy if desired.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Prefer the validated candidate command when it is marked valid and the system is not faulted; otherwise drive the deterministic fallback command. Deassert act_enable in fault/fallback conditions unless the design is explicitly configured to hold last-safe command.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Keep only minimal state for any optional rate-limiting or last-safe behavior; otherwise remain primarily feed-through from validated inputs to bounded outputs with reset-safe defaults.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Clamp the selected command to [actuator_min, actuator_max], assert clamp_active when clamping occurs, and drive fallback_active_out whenever safe fallback is being output; ensure deterministic act_cmd and act_enable under reset or invalid input.
ownership_notes: Owns the final bounded actuator command and enable output.
Consumes only validated candidate command, fallback command, and safety flags; it does not inspect raw transport metadata.
Must preserve deterministic safe behavior on reset, missing candidate data, or fault conditions.

fsm_intent.description: No explicit complex FSM is required beyond synchronous register updates, request-pending tracking, watchdog timing, and safe fallback selection. A small implicit lifecycle is sufficient: reset/safe, configured/idle, request outstanding, response validate, and fallback/fault handling.
Use direct address decode and registered side effects rather than a multi-state FSM; writes and reads are qualified by the bus strobes.
Use a simple synchronous request/response lifecycle with request accept, watchdog count, response check, and fallback/fault assertion; avoid a complicated FSM.
No explicit FSM is required; output selection can be implemented as straightforward conditional logic with optional registered last-safe state if used.

inputs: semantic control outputs from register map
internal_storage: optional small FIFO/BRAM if needed for timing closure
output_mapping: telemetry outputs from the owning submodules
semantic control outputs and diagnostic mirrors

internal_storage: optional last-safe command register if rate limiting or hold-last-safe behavior is used

sequencing_notes: Configuration writes only take effect when cfg_valid and cfg_write are asserted with cfg_ready high; reads only return valid data when cfg_valid and cfg_read are asserted.
A request acceptance event is req_valid && req_ready; on that event the transport captures transaction ID and starts the watchdog.
A response is only consumed for control if rsp_valid is asserted and the parsed fields satisfy transaction ID match, freshness limit, legal status, and parser checks.
Fault conditions force fallback immediately or on the next synchronous update, with sticky faults retained until clear_faults is written and the active fault condition has cleared.
The actuator path should clamp after selecting the candidate or fallback command, then drive act_cmd and act_enable according to safe-state policy.
timing_notes: Use a single clk domain with fully synchronous state updates.
Prefer simple registered control paths and combinational decode where possible to keep timing predictable.
If bulk history/FIFO storage is needed, implement it with inferred or vendor block RAM via a technology-neutral wrapper, not flattened registers.
Keep top-level buses at 64 bits or less and maintain a compact pinout under the stated limit.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
